item.title: Tsuruoka: Chido Museum & the Shonai Samurai Town — Guide
item.description: Tsuruoka was the castle town of the powerful Shonai Domain and retains an exceptional stock of Meiji-era Western-style buildings and samurai residences. The Chido Museum gathers relocated historical structures — samurai houses, a former prefectural office and a police station — in a parkland setting. The nearby Zenpoji Temple complex and Tsuruoka Catholic Church (1903) add to a remarkably diverse historic townscape. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Tsuruoka, Yamagata Hours Museum ~9:00–16:30 Admission Around ¥700 Time needed About 2 hours Best time Year-round What to See Relocated samurai residences at the Chido Museum.

item.title: Osaka Kendo Class Guide: Try the Way of the Sword
item.description: Behind the thunderous shouts and clashing bamboo of a dojo lies kendo — “the way of the sword,” the modern martial art descended from samurai swordsmanship. A kendo experience class in Osaka lets visitors step onto the dojo floor, grip the bamboo shinai, learn a few basic cuts and stances, and even try on a piece of the armour, all under an instructor who explains the discipline, spirit, and etiquette behind it.

item.title: Toei Kyoto Studio Park (Uzumasa Eigamura) Guide: Step Into a Samurai Movie
item.description: Part working film studio, part theme park, Toei Kyoto Studio Park (Uzumasa Eigamura) lets you walk straight into a samurai movie. Built around the back-lot sets where countless Japanese period dramas (jidaigeki) have been filmed, it recreates the streets of Edo-period Japan — wooden shopfronts, a Nihonbashi bridge, a red-light district, a courthouse — complete with costumed actors, live ninja and samurai sword shows, and the chance to dress up as a samurai, ninja, or even an oiran courtesan.

item.title: Kochi Hidden Gems: Niyodo River, Aki Samurai District & Washi Paper
item.description: Most visitors who come to Kochi arrive with Kochi Castle, katsuo tataki, and perhaps the Shimanto River already in mind. These are not wrong choices — each is genuinely worth the trip. But Kochi is an unusually large prefecture, the largest in Shikoku by area, and its size conceals a range of experiences that the standard itinerary entirely misses. The river with the most extraordinary water colour in Japan is not the Shimanto but the Niyodo, accessible by road an hour from Kochi City.
